title: 03 — Building a Chatbot
html:
03 — Building a Chatbot

The one idea: a useful chatbot is mostly not the model. It is a conversation store, a retrieval step that supplies trusted sources, a policy for what to do when it doesn't know, a handoff to a person, and measurement. The model writes the sentences. The system decides what it is allowed to say.

1. What it is

Type What it does Example
FAQ or knowledge bot Answers from approved documents, with citations "Why is the direct plan cheaper?"
Task bot Takes actions through tools, with confirmation "Update my nominee", "download my statement"
Internal copilot Helps staff search, summarise and draft "Summarise this rating rationale"
Agentic assistant Plans multi-step work with many tools (05) "Prepare the monthly exceptions report"

Start with the simplest type that meets the need. Most business value is in the first two.

2. Why it matters

  • People trust a chatbot's tone more than its accuracy. One confident wrong answer about money or rules does real harm.
  • Regulated domains need sources, refusal and escalation, not creativity.
  • Without measurement, every prompt change is a guess (08).

3. The main ideas

3.1 Architecture

---
title: Chatbot reference architecture
---
flowchart LR
    U["User<br/>(web, app, Teams, WhatsApp)"] --> API["Chat API<br/>(auth, rate limits)"]
    API --> ST["Conversation store<br/>(turns, summaries)"]
    API --> IN["Input checks<br/>(injection, PII, topic)"]
    IN --> RET["Retrieve sources<br/>(hybrid search over approved docs)"]
    RET --> LLM["Model call<br/>(system prompt + trimmed history + sources)"]
    LLM --> OUT["Output checks<br/>(citations, PII, safe rendering)"]
    OUT --> U
    OUT -- "not grounded / user asks" --> H["Human handoff<br/>(ticket or live agent)"]
    LLM -. "tools" .-> T["Actions behind confirmation"]
    API --> LOG["Traces, feedback, evals"]

3.2 Conversation state

  • The API is stateless. Store turns yourself (a database, or Redis for sessions), keyed by user and conversation.
  • Budget the context: keep the system prompt, the most recent turns, and a running summary of older turns. Trim from the oldest.
  • Long conversations: some APIs offer server-side compaction (Claude's compaction beta summarises earlier context automatically). Otherwise, summarise yourself every N turns.
  • Memory across sessions (preferences, facts the user told you): store it explicitly, scoped to the user, with an expiry, and let users see and delete it.

3.3 Grounding and refusal

  1. Retrieve passages from approved sources only, each with an id and date.
  2. The system prompt says: answer only from the sources, cite them, and say you don't know otherwise.
  3. Check the answer: does it cite? Do the cited ids exist? If not, replace it with a safe fallback.
  4. Offer a person when the bot can't answer, when the user asks, or when the topic is sensitive (complaints, advice, account changes).

3.4 Channels and deployment

Channel Build with
Website or app Your own UI with streaming (SSE or WebSocket) from an ASP.NET Core or FastAPI backend
Microsoft Teams The Microsoft 365 Agents SDK or Teams AI tooling (check current Microsoft docs)
WhatsApp and SMS The Meta WhatsApp Business Platform or a provider such as Twilio
Phone A voice assistant (06)

Deploy the chat API like any service: container, autoscaling, secrets in a vault, logs and traces, rate limits per user.

4. Working code

The script implements the core loop with a stand-in model: retrieve from a tiny knowledge base, answer only with a citation or hand off, and keep conversation context within a token budget. Standard library only.

import re

# A support chatbot's core loop, with a stand-in for the model so it runs offline.
KNOWLEDGE = {  # retrieved passages would normally come from a search index, each with a source
    "kb-12": "Direct plans have a lower expense ratio than regular plans because no distributor commission is paid.",
    "kb-31": "NAVs are published every business day after markets close.",
    "kb-40": "To change a nominee, submit the nominee form through your account settings.",
}
words = lambda s: set(re.findall(r"[a-z]+", s.lower())) - {"the", "a", "is", "are", "of", "to", "my", "do", "i", "how", "what", "when", "than"}

def retrieve(question, k=1, min_overlap=2):
    scored = sorted(((len(words(question) & words(t)), sid) for sid, t in KNOWLEDGE.items()), reverse=True)
    return [(sid, KNOWLEDGE[sid]) for score, sid in scored[:k] if score >= min_overlap]

def fake_model(system, history, passages):
    # A real model would write the answer. This stand-in only shows the contract:
    # answer from passages with a citation, or say it doesn't know.
    if not passages:
        return "I don't have that in my sources. I can connect you to a person. [handoff]"
    sid, text = passages[0]
    return f"{text} [source: {sid}]"

class Conversation:
    def __init__(self, system, max_tokens=60):
        self.system, self.turns, self.max_tokens = system, [], max_tokens
    def tokens(self, text):                     # rough estimate: 1 token per 0.75 words
        return int(len(text.split()) / 0.75) + 1
    def trimmed(self):                          # keep the most recent turns that fit the budget
        kept, used = [], self.tokens(self.system)
        for role, text in reversed(self.turns):
            if used + self.tokens(text) > self.max_tokens:
                break
            kept.insert(0, (role, text)); used += self.tokens(text)
        return kept, used
    def ask(self, question):
        self.turns.append(("user", question))
        history, used = self.trimmed()
        answer = fake_model(self.system, history, retrieve(question))
        self.turns.append(("assistant", answer))
        return answer, len(history), used

chat = Conversation(system="Answer only from the provided sources. Cite them. Offer a person when unsure.")
for q in ["Why is the direct plan expense ratio lower than regular plans?",
          "When are NAVs published each business day?",
          "Can you predict next month's return of my fund?",
          "How do I change the nominee on my account?"]:
    answer, kept, used = chat.ask(q)
    print(f"Q: {q}\nA: {answer}\n   (context kept: {kept} turns, ~{used} tokens)")

Output:

Q: Why is the direct plan expense ratio lower than regular plans?
A: Direct plans have a lower expense ratio than regular plans because no distributor commission is paid. [source: kb-12]
   (context kept: 1 turns, ~33 tokens)
Q: When are NAVs published each business day?
A: NAVs are published every business day after markets close. [source: kb-31]
   (context kept: 2 turns, ~53 tokens)
Q: Can you predict next month's return of my fund?
A: I don't have that in my sources. I can connect you to a person. [handoff]
   (context kept: 3 turns, ~56 tokens)
Q: How do I change the nominee on my account?
A: To change a nominee, submit the nominee form through your account settings. [source: kb-40]
   (context kept: 2 turns, ~52 tokens)

What to notice:

  • Every factual answer carries a source id. The return-prediction question matches no source, so the bot hands off instead of guessing.
  • Context stays under the 60-token budget. By the fourth question, the oldest turns are dropped (2 turns kept). A real bot would also keep a summary of what was dropped.

The real model call slots into fake_model: build the messages from history, add the passages to the user turn with their ids, and call the API as in 02.

5. Common mistakes

  1. No "I don't know" path. The model fills gaps confidently.
  2. Retrieving from unapproved or stale sources. Index only reviewed documents, with dates.
  3. Unbounded history. Cost and latency grow every turn.
  4. Actions without confirmation. Any change to an account needs an explicit "yes" from the user.
  5. No feedback loop. Collect thumbs up and down with the conversation id, and review them weekly.

6. Exercise (2 hours)

  1. Add a summary: when turns are trimmed, keep a one-line summary of them in the context.
  2. Add a topic filter that hands off on "complaint" or "advice" without calling the model.
  3. Replace fake_model with a real API call, and compare the answers with and without the "only from sources" instruction.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Where does conversation state live, and why?
  2. What three things make an answer "grounded"?
  3. When should a chatbot hand off to a person?
  4. How do you keep long conversations affordable?
  5. Why must actions require confirmation?

Answers

  1. In your own store, because the model API is stateless and you need control over retention, privacy and trimming.
  2. It comes from approved sources, cites them, and the citations check out.
  3. When it can't answer from sources, when the user asks, and for sensitive topics such as complaints, advice and account changes.
  4. Trim old turns, keep a running summary, cache the stable prefix, and use compaction where the API offers it.
  5. Model output is probabilistic and can be manipulated. A person must confirm anything that changes the real world.
